title: HDFC Bank snaps three-day losses, rises nearly 1%: This analyst sees three upside triggers for the heavyweight stock- Moneycontrol.com
text:

'We believe the current valuation (of HDFC Bank) already discounts a significant portion of the negative news,' an analyst says   September 10, 2026 / 17:11 IST             HDFC Bank shares snapped three-day losses and were trading nearly 1% higher on September 10. An analyst sees three upside triggers for the heavyweight stock that could revive its fortunes after the stock hit fresh 52-week-low recently. "We see three key triggers: CEO succession clarity, resolution of the US legal case and NIM stabilisation. We expect Kaizad Bharucha to take over as CEO for the next three-year term, which should provide leadership continuity and improve investor confidence. Further improvement in deposits and normalisation of the credit-deposit ratio could provide additional support. "At current valuations, we see an attractive risk-reward. We believe fundamental downside is relatively limited, while the stock offers meaningful upside if investor confidence improves and valuations move closer to historical levels. In our view, most current concerns are transitional rather than structural. Strong fundamentals, improved funding, better operating KPIs and a potential valuation re-rating could support the next leg of HDFC Bank’s performance," said Abhinav Tiwari, Senior Research Analyst at Bonanza. "We remain positive on HDFC Bank and believe the recent weakness in the stock has created an attractive entry opportunity. The stock has been impacted by concerns around CEO succession, Atanu Chakraborty’s resignation, Credit Suisse AT1 bonds, the Rs 45 crore MSRDC arrangement and an ongoing US investor related legal case. These developments have weakened investor sentiment and resulted in a sharp valuation de rating. However, we believe the market is currently pricing these issues as a larger governance concern than the underlying facts suggest. Reviews and investigations have not indicated any mala fide intent, personal enrichment or systemic governance failure. While there is room to improve processes, we do not believe these issues weaken HDFC Bank’s core franchise," he added. The analyst also weighed on the private lender's valuation. "HDFC Bank has raised around $12 billion through FCNR(B) deposits at 6.25%, which is a positive for its liability franchise. The additional foreign-currency funding provides balance-sheet flexibility and helps address the credit-deposit mismatch that emerged after the HDFC Ltd merger. It should also reduce pressure on domestic deposit mobilisation and support future  loan  growth. Valuation is a key part of our investment thesis. HDFC Bank has historically traded at a premium due to its strong asset quality, retail and MSME franchise, robust liability franchise and consistent return ratios. However, the stock is currently trading at around 1.8x P/B, close to a multi-year low, compared with its historical trading range of above 2.5x P/B. We believe the current valuation already discounts a significant portion of the negative news. The challenges following the HDFC Ltd merger are gradually being addressed, while the recent concerns have further depressed investor sentiment," Tiwari further said. At 2:50 pm on September 10,  HDFC Bank shares  were trading 0.8% higher at Rs 692.3 apiece. Meanwhile, another analyst said the heavyweight stock is in a "clear weekly downtrend". "HDFC Bank remains in a clear weekly downtrend, with price trading below major EMAs and facing rejection near ₹840. Momentum remains weak, while ₹683 is the key support. Avoid fresh buying; existing positions should be monitored closely, with Rs 683–675 as the major support zone. A breakdown below ₹683 can open Rs 636–625," said Virat Jagad, Senior Technical Research Analyst at Bonanza. "Heavyweight private lender HDFC Bank continues to remain locked in a strong downward trajectory, extending its prolonged weakness from late 2025 into the current trading sessions. Technical charts indicate a consistent series of lower highs and lower lows, with the stock trading well below its major key moving averages—including the 20-day, 50-day, and 200-day Simple Moving Averages (SMAs). Sustained selling pressure and negative price momentum have dragged the stock toward a crucial historic demand zone. Prices are now approaching a strong previous support band situated near the Rs 650 – Rs 630 level, an area that may expect a potential floor or trigger short-term buying interest. "Prospective buyers and new investors should adopt a 'wait-and-watch' stance as the stock remains firmly entrenched in a bearish trend. Buying at current levels carries heightened risk without clear confirmation of a reversal. Investors should monitor for signs of a bounce or consolidation near the Rs 650 – Rs 630 support zone. A favourable long entry opens up only if the price stabilises and reclaims its key moving averages. Any fresh positions strictly require a well-defined stop-loss and a prudent risk-reward ratio," said Mayank Jain, Market Analyst, Share.Market by PhonePe.
